message.content:
Fresh-context review; read only, never build or run cargo/just (another process is building in that worktree). Worktree: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/wp-q-verify-real. Run `/usr/bin/git diff origin/main` plus read the untracked files crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_verify_real.rs and crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/local_registries.rs.

Finding being addressed: callisto has no recovery evidence against real registries; the https-only rule in crates/callisto-graph/src/registry_endpoint.rs blocks binding local registries. Chosen fix: no production change; local registries serve self-signed TLS so `[registries.npm]`/`[registries.pypi]` bind through production binding. `just verify-real` must exit nonzero on any wrong outcome across: partial publish -> rerun adopts, delayed visibility, conflicting tag, missing Python artifact. Cargo cannot be rehearsed (callisto always passes `--registry crates-io`); that is documented, not a bug to flag.

Look for: tests that would pass even if callisto behaved wrongly (weak assertions, a scenario that does not prove its claim), flakiness (ports, timing, sleeps), leaked server processes, shell/justfile errors, CI action breakage (.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml now calls `just verify-real-tools`), violations of AGENTS.md (no unwrap outside tests is fine in tests; terse one-line comments; no history words; no emojis), and behavior regressions in the refactored release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs (helpers moved into common/local_registries.rs). Report only issues you can justify from the code, each with file:line and a concrete failure scenario. Under 40 lines.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

--- a/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml

@@ -1,23 +1,14 @@
 name: 'Install registry test tools'

-      shell: bash
-      # legacy-cgi: pypiserver imports `cgi` (gone in 3.13). gunicorn: avoids a slow getfqdn() bind.
-      # setuptools/wheel: the test builds with `--no-isolation`, so they must be pre-installed.

-        python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv"
-        "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin/pip" install pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1

-      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
-      shell: bash
-      run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
+      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entries are fixed children of the checkout, not attacker-controlled input.
+        just verify-real-tools
+        for dir in venv/bin npm/node_modules/.bin cargo/bin; do
+          echo "$PWD/target/verify-real/$dir" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
+        done
diff --git a/AGENTS.md b/AGENTS.md
index cd5a66505..b16888ab8 100644
--- a/AGENTS.md
+++ b/AGENTS.md
@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@ Rules for AI agents working in this repo.
 
 - Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
 - Before every push or PR: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, and `just ci` before marking a PR ready. Judge each by its exit code. Never tail or grep the output for success (a compile error prints no "failed" line), and never report a check as passed that was not run.
+- Recovery evidence: `just verify-real` rehearses partial publish, delayed visibility, a conflicting tag and a missing Python artifact against local npm and PyPI registries bound over self-signed `https://` through `[registries]`. It installs its tools under `target/verify-real` and is not part of `just ci`. A local Cargo registry cannot be bound: callisto always publishes with `--registry crates-io`.
 - Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
 - Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
 - Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
diff --git a/docs/architecture/release.md b/docs/architecture/release.md
index 31559e357..764025d44 100644
--- a/docs/architecture/release.md
+++ b/docs/architecture/release.md
@@ -140,3 +140,5 @@ Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fiel
 Downloaded binaries are checked with `gh attestation verify` against `orin-dx/callisto`, the `callisto-release.yml` signer and the `refs/heads/main` source ref before extraction. Only the `callisto` binary is extracted. `verification: require` aborts on failure; `fallback` (default) deletes the asset and installs from crates.io; `skip` warns and uses it. Fallback pins the requested version except for `latest`. Older unattested releases motivate the default. `require` and `fallback` never run an unverified asset.
 
 Product assets target `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. The Intel macOS asset is cross-compiled on an Apple silicon runner, and the arm64 Linux asset is built natively on an arm64 runner. Apple signing and notarization are out of scope. GitHub provenance binds assets to the orchestration revision; the intent and artifact manifest bind their bytes to the release source. Callisto publishes its crates to crates.io and product assets to GitHub Releases, not to another registry for rehearsal.
+
+`just verify-real` rehearses recovery against local registries through the production registry binding, with no test-only allowance in the https rule: Verdaccio, `pypiserver` and a JSON simple index serve a self-signed loopback certificate that npm, curl and Twine trust through their own CA variables. The rehearsals are a partial npm publish adopted by a rerun, a PyPI index that shows an upload late or never, a remote tag on another commit, and a PyPI release whose index lacks one built file. Cargo is not rehearsed: its publish and observation always name the `crates-io` registry, which cannot be pointed at a local one.
diff --git a/justfile b/justfile
index 06542f0ff..6998ceca1 100644
--- a/justfile
+++ b/justfile
@@ -120,6 +120,26 @@ features-boundary:
     if [ -z "$tree" ]; then echo "cargo tree printed nothing" >&2; exit 1; fi
     if grep 'test-util' <<<"$tree"; then exit 1; fi
 
+# The local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry suites run against, installed under target/verify-real.
+# gunicorn: pypiserver's default backend does a slow getfqdn() bind. setuptools and wheel: the offline Python build.
+verify-real-tools:
+    #!/usr/bin/env bash
+    tools=target/verify-real
+    mkdir -p "$tools"
+    npm install --silent --no-audit --no-fund --prefix "$tools/npm" verdaccio@6.10.4
+    if command -v uv >/dev/null; then uv venv -q --allow-existing --python 3.12 "$tools/venv"; else python3 -m venv "$tools/venv"; fi
+    python_pins="pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1"
+    "$tools/venv/bin/python" -m pip install -q $python_pins
+    "$tools/venv/bin/python" -m pip download -q -d "$tools/wheels" setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
+    cargo install --locked --root "$tools/cargo" cargo-http-registry@0.1.8
+
+# Rehearses partial publish, delayed visibility, a conflicting tag and a missing Python artifact against local registries.
+verify-real: verify-real-tools
+    #!/usr/bin/env bash
+    tools="$PWD/target/verify-real"
+    export PATH="$tools/venv/bin:$tools/npm/node_modules/.bin:$tools/cargo/bin:$PATH"
+    VERIFY_REAL_WHEELS="$tools/wheels" cargo test -p callisto-cli --test release_verify_real -- --ignored --test-threads=1
+
 # Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
 machete:
     cargo machete

file.content:
set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]

# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Time `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and count their git processes.
# `CALLISTO_BENCH_PACKAGES=50,200` picks the sizes.
bench:
    cargo bench -p callisto-cli --bench commands

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's shell block with Git and GitHub faked; it never calls the real binary (see test-release-action-binary).
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and feeds its real error output through the CI problem matcher.
test-problem-matcher:
    bash .github/tests/test-problem-matcher.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Reject history words and plain comment blocks over three lines (`comment-block-ok` marks an exception).
check-comments:
    bash testing/check-comments.sh

# Clippy as one workspace invocation: moon's per-project runs serialize on cargo's shared target/ lock.
lint: check-comments
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Lint only moon-affected projects, in one cargo invocation to avoid the build-lock serialization.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit: license-boundary
    cargo deny check

# callisto-model is MIT: nothing it depends on at build or run time, directly or not, may be FSL-licensed or a Callisto FSL crate.
license-boundary:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    tree=$(cargo tree -p callisto-model -e normal,build --prefix none --format '{p} {l}')
    if [ -z "$tree" ]; then echo "cargo tree printed nothing" >&2; exit 1; fi
    if grep -E 'FSL|callisto-(manifests|graph|cli|fixtures)' <<<"$tree"; then exit 1; fi

# Compile the fuzz targets so they cannot rot (running them needs nightly and cargo-fuzz)
fuzz-check:
    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# The shipped binary is built with the features its crates default to, and none of them is the dev-only `test-util`.
features-boundary:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    tree=$(cargo tree -p callisto-cli -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}')
    if [ -z "$tree" ]; then echo "cargo tree printed nothing" >&2; exit 1; fi
    if grep 'test-util' <<<"$tree"; then exit 1; fi

# The local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry suites run against, installed under target/verify-real.
# gunicorn: pypiserver's default backend does a slow getfqdn() bind. setuptools and wheel: the offline Python build.
verify-real-tools:

input.message:
Read-only review of the wp-q-verify-real diff against origin/main plus the two untracked files. I built and ran nothing. Findings, most severe first:

1. **justfile:125-134 and 137-142 (both new recipes): failures are silently swallowed.** Every other shebang recipe starts with `set -euo pipefail` (lines 76, 102, 118); these two do not, so only the last command's exit code counts.
   - `verify-real-tools` can exit 0 after a failed `npm install`, `pip install` or `pip download`, as long as the final `cargo install` succeeds.
   - Concrete case: wherever `uv` is on PATH, `uv venv` creates a venv without pip (that needs `--seed`). `python -m pip install` then fails with "No module named pip", and the recipe still exits 0.
   - Downstream effect: `just verify-real` then fails later with a confusing "gunicorn must be spawnable". The CI step in `.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml` reports green and only the e2e tests fail later.
   - Fix: add `set -euo pipefail` and pass `--seed` to `uv venv`.
2. **release_verify_real.rs:411 (missing-wheel test): flaky.** The mirror copies the wheel the moment it appears in pypiserver's store (`Duration::ZERO`), while pypiserver may still be writing it.
   - The index then serves a truncated copy. `copy_missing` never replaces an existing file, so the truncation is permanent.
   - Because the wheel is in this run's uploaded list, `pypi_files::compare` marks it as differing, and `confirm` returns a hard `PypiFileDiffers` error (pypi.rs:464).
   - Lines 285 and 359 have the same non-atomic `fs::copy` while the index is being polled.
   - Fix: wait a short settle time, and copy to a temp name then rename.
3. **release_verify_real.rs:361-368 (delayed index): the timing assertion proves nothing.** `started` is taken before `execute`, which includes the Python build and upload, so `elapsed > 2500ms` holds whether or not callisto ever saw the index empty.
   - Completion only proves recovery if a confirm look happened inside the 2.5 s window. If callisto first looked after 2.5 s, the test still passes without exercising delayed visibility.
   - The index script's `log_message` is a no-op, so nothing records the miss.
   - Fix: log requests in the index script and assert at least one 404 after the upload.
4. **release_verify_real.rs:198-218 (conflicting tag): does not check that nothing was published.** It asserts E167 and an unchanged tag only.
   - If callisto published both npm packages and only then hit the tag conflict, the test still passes.
   - Fix: add `assert!(npm.versions(DEPENDENCY).is_empty())` and the same for DEPENDENT, if stopping before any publish is the intended behavior.
5. **release_verify_real.rs:234 plus local_registries.rs:29: port races.**
   - Two `free_loopback_port()` calls each bind and release, so they can return the same port. `wait_for_port` then succeeds against the JSON index even though gunicorn failed to bind, and Twine uploads to the wrong server.
   - Ports are also chosen before fixture creation (seconds of callisto runs), which widens the gap before another process takes the port.
   - Fix: hold both listeners until both ports have been read.
6. **release_verify_real.rs:291-298: slow failures, not wrong results.** `after` waits up to 60 s even when the run has already failed, and `mirror.join().unwrap()` runs before the release assertions. A failed second run therefore stalls for 60 s before reporting.

Checked and fine:
- The partial-publish test: the registry-state checks and the "already published" warning match `release_execution.rs:102`.
- The never-shows rerun: pypiserver refuses to overwrite and callisto passes no `--skip-existing`, so a re-upload would fail the run.
- The `ServerGuard` cleanup.

Read-only review of the wp-q-verify-real diff against origin/main plus the two untracked files. I built and ran nothing. Findings, most severe first:

1. **justfile:125-134 and 137-142 (both new recipes): failures are silently swallowed.** Every other shebang recipe starts with `set -euo pipefail` (lines 76, 102, 118); these two do not, so only the last command's exit code counts.
   - `verify-real-tools` can exit 0 after a failed `npm install`, `pip install` or `pip download`, as long as the final `cargo install` succeeds.
   - Concrete case: wherever `uv` is on PATH, `uv venv` creates a venv without pip (that needs `--seed`). `python -m pip install` then fails with "No module named pip", and the recipe still exits 0.
   - Downstream effect: `just verify-real` then fails later with a confusing "gunicorn must be spawnable". The CI step in `.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml` reports green and only the e2e tests fail later.
   - Fix: add `set -euo pipefail` and pass `--seed` to `uv venv`.
2. **release_verify_real.rs:411 (missing-wheel test): flaky.** The mirror copies the wheel the moment it appears in pypiserver's store (`Duration::ZERO`), while pypiserver may still be writing it.
   - The index then serves a truncated copy. `copy_missing` never replaces an existing file, so the truncation is permanent.
   - Because the wheel is in this run's uploaded list, `pypi_files::compare` marks it as differing, and `confirm` returns a hard `PypiFileDiffers` error (pypi.rs:464).
   - Lines 285 and 359 have the same non-atomic `fs::copy` while the index is being polled.
   - Fix: wait a short settle time, and copy to a temp name then rename.
3. **release_verify_real.rs:361-368 (delayed index): the timing assertion proves nothing.** `started` is taken before `execute`, which includes the Python build and upload, so `elapsed > 2500ms` holds whether or not callisto ever saw the index empty.
   - Completion only proves recovery if a confirm look happened inside the 2.5 s window. If callisto first looked after 2.5 s, the test still passes without exercising delayed visibility.
   - The index script's `log_message` is a no-op, so nothing records the miss.
   - Fix: log requests in the index script and assert at least one 404 after the upload.
4. **release_verify_real.rs:198-218 (conflicting tag): does not check that nothing was published.** It asserts E167 and an unchanged tag only.
   - If callisto published both npm packages and only then hit the tag conflict, the test still passes.
   - Fix: add `assert!(npm.versions(DEPENDENCY).is_empty())` and the same for DEPENDENT, if stopping before any publish is the intended behavior.
5. **release_verify_real.rs:234 plus local_registries.rs:29: port races.**
   - Two `free_loopback_port()` calls each bind and release, so they can return the same port. `wait_for_port` then succeeds against the JSON index even though gunicorn failed to bind, and Twine uploads to the wrong server.
   - Ports are also chosen before fixture creation (seconds of callisto runs), which widens the gap before another process takes the port.
   - Fix: hold both listeners until both ports have been read.
6. **release_verify_real.rs:291-298: slow failures, not wrong results.** `after` waits up to 60 s even when the run has already failed, and `mirror.join().unwrap()` runs before the release assertions. A failed second run therefore stalls for 60 s before reporting.

Checked and fine:
- The partial-publish test: the registry-state checks and the "already published" warning match `release_execution.rs:102`.
- The never-shows rerun: pypiserver refuses to overwrite and callisto passes no `--skip-existing`, so a re-upload would fail the run.
- The `ServerGuard` cleanup.

- `just` is installed before the action in both workflows (callisto-ci.yml:119, callisto-release.yml:42).
- The e2e refactor keeps the old behavior: the HTTP pypiserver path and the Verdaccio `listen:` config replacing `-l`.
